title: In an abstract ring, x*(-1)=-x
statement: For any ring record R (an abstract carrier, additive/multiplicative structure, negation) and element x of R's carrier, mul x (neg one) = neg x.

formal.statement: theorem Alg.mul_neg_one : ((x0 : Alg.Ring) -> ((x1 : Alg.Ring.carrier x0) -> Eq.{1} (Alg.Ring.carrier x0) (Alg.Ring.mul x0 x1 (Alg.Ring.neg x0 (Alg.Ring.one x0))) (Alg.Ring.neg x0 x1)))

evidence.supports: Alg.mul_neg_one admits through the trusted kernel gate. Built by projecting R's additive structure to a Group (Ring.toCommGroup then CommGroup.toGroup -- the payoff Alg.CommMonoid.toMonoid/etc exist for) and applying Alg.groupInvUnique there at (x, mul x (neg one), neg x), rather than deriving `mul a (neg b) = neg (mul a b)` directly. FACT1 (add (mul x (neg one)) x = zero) is derived from distribL, Alg.ringMulZero, and mulOneR; FACT2 is R.negAdd x directly. Type-checks symbolically (closed over free x) at both Int.ring and Rat.ring.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- sub_self_and_mul_neg_one_apply_symbolically_at_int_and_rat_rings --nocapture --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out"| grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

evidence.supports: NO retirement target under this exact name/direction on either carrier: Int's `neg_one_mul` is the MIRRORED LEFT form ((-1)*x=-x, not x*(-1)=-x) and Rat has no `mul_neg_one`/`neg_one_mul` at all. Bridging the two directions needs mul_comm (a CommRing fact this theorem is deliberately stated without, since it is proved at the Ring level). Confirmed by a compiled reference to Int.neg_one_mul (a field that would fail to compile if renamed/removed), not by a text grep alone.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- mul_neg_one_has_no_retirement_target --nocapture --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out"| grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

notes: Not a retirement of anything: this is a NEW fact at both Int and Rat. Stated at Ring (no commutativity assumed) -- the RIGHT-multiplication direction; a symmetric LEFT-multiplication statement is a separate theorem this lane did not build.
